title: The Origins of Breakfast Foods
summary: Josh and Chuck mark episode 1500 with thanks to listeners, staff and families, then explore the origins of Western breakfast foods. Topics include the etymology and religious roots of "breakfast," the historical role of alcohol and savory foods at breakfast, the Beech-Nut bacon ad campaign, bagels (origin of the word, Polish and Jewish history in the US, mass production, lox vs. smoked salmon), oatmeal (groats, rolled oats, Quaker Oats, the Quaker Man figure), coffee and orange juice (Minute Maid frozen concentrate, the 1916 orange campaign), pancakes, waffles (Catholic Church wafer-irons, Cornelius Swartwout patent, National Waffle Day), French toast (pain perdue, "poor knights of Windsor"), and brunch (Guy Barringer's 1895 essay, Hollywood, post-WWII church attendance). The episode closes with a listener email about mangroves in Minecraft.

segments.title: Episode 1500 acknowledgement and opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts note that this is episode 1500, thank staff, listeners and families, and introduce the idea of a breakfast topic.

segments.title: Origins of breakfast and the word breakfast
segments.summary: The hosts explain the meaning of breakfast as breaking a fast, its religious roots tied to waiting for communion, and how breakfast customs varied, including alcohol and savory meals in earlier centuries and in Japan today.

segments.title: Eggs, bacon and the Beech-Nut campaign
segments.summary: Eggs have long been eaten at breakfast. Industrialization made quick breakfasts common. Beech-Nut worked with Edward Bernays on a campaign promoting bacon and big breakfasts, which helped make breakfast seem most important meal of the day.

segments.title: Bagels: history, name origin and spread in America
segments.summary: The hosts discuss personal bagel preferences and then the origin of the word bagel, with the earliest printed use from 1610 in Krakow, and how Jewish immigrants brought bagels to New York. Mass-production machines in the 1950s by Harry and Murray Lender helped them spread.

segments.title: Lox, smoked salmon and bagel toppings
segments.summary: The hosts compare lox with smoked salmon, noting lox is salt-cured and smoked salmon is lighter on salt. They mention cream cheese and lox popularized by Family Circle magazine.

segments.title: Oatmeal, groats, rolled oats and Quaker Oats
segments.summary: Oats were domesticated late and eaten as groats until rancidity problems led Henry Seymour and William Heston to develop rolled oats, the basis of Quaker Oats. The hosts discuss the Quaker Man logo and the flavored packets.

segments.title: Coffee, orange juice and frozen concentrate
segments.summary: Coffee's origin legend involving an Ethiopian goat herder is recounted, and coffee replaced alcohol as a breakfast drink. Orange juice became a breakfast staple through a 1916 promotion and trains, and frozen concentrate by Minute Maid was developed for US soldiers in the 1940s.

segments.title: Pancakes, waffles and National Waffle Day
segments.summary: Pancakes are likely among the oldest breakfasts, with evidence in Ice Man's stomach. Regional pancake variations are described. Waffles trace from ancient Greek obelios and medieval Church wafer irons to Cornelius Swartwout's 1869 patent, with National Waffle Day on August 24, and Thomas Jefferson's supposed importation of waffle irons. Shrove Tuesday pancakes are also mentioned.

segments.title: French toast, pain perdue and poor knights of Windsor
segments.summary: The hosts discuss French toast, the legend of innkeeper Joseph French, the first recorded use in 1660, the French name pain perdue, and the British name poor knights of Windsor with competing explanations.

segments.title: Brunch origins and history
segments.summary: Brunch is traced to Guy Barringer's essay 'Brunch: A Plea,' with earlier English hunt breakfasts as precursors. Brunch spread in the US in the 1930s via Hollywood and grew after World War Two as church attendance declined. Blunch was a proposed alternative name.

segments.title: Listener mail: Minecraft mangroves
segments.summary: A listener writes that a Minecraft update added mangrove swamps with red mangrove root blocks and propagules, relating to the earlier mangrove episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank the listener and invite listener emails about things they should know.
